If a tool returns an error, try a different tool or different arguments instead of repeating the call, and never repeat a call that already succeeded. When every step is covered, stop calling tools and reply with two or three sentences on what you gathered and any step you could not cover.

messages.content:
Research AAPL for an investment report.

Research plan:
1. Establish current price momentum and technical backdrop (suggested tools: get_price_summary, get_price_history)
2. Assess company fundamentals, valuation multiples, and historical context (suggested tools: get_company_info, get_financials)
3. Evaluate recent earnings performance vs. expectations and trend (suggested tools: get_earnings, get_recent_filings)
4. Analyze recent news flow and investor sentiment (suggested tools: get_news_digest, get_news)
5. Understand the macroeconomic environment and its relevance to AAPL (suggested tools: get_macro_snapshot, get_series)
6. Review latest 10-Q or 10-K filing for forward guidance, risks, and capital allocation (suggested tools: get_filing_text)
7. Synthesize findings into catalysts, risks, and Buy/Hold/Sell recommendation

Work through every step with the tools.

tools.name: get_company_info
tools.description:
Company profile and key valuation metrics.

Returns name, sector, industry, market cap, P/E ratios, margins,
growth, beta, analyst recommendation and target price, and a short
business description. Use at the start of research to understand
what the company does.

Args:
    ticker: Stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL".

tools.name: get_price_summary
tools.description:
Recent stock performance at a glance.

Returns the last close, 1m/3m/6m/1y returns (as fractions, 0.05 =
5%), 52-week high and low, and annualized volatility. Use this first
when assessing how a stock has been trading.

Args:
    ticker: Stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL".

tools.name: get_price_history
tools.description:
Daily (or other interval) OHLCV price history for a stock.

Use when you need raw prices, e.g. to chart a stock or compute your
own statistics. For a quick read on performance use
get_price_summary instead.

Args:
    ticker: Stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL".
    period: yfinance period: 1mo, 3mo, 6mo, 1y, 2y, 5y, ytd, max.
    interval: 1d, 1wk, or 1mo.

tools.name: get_financials
tools.description:
Key lines from the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow.

Covers revenue, gross profit, operating income, net income, EPS,
EBITDA, assets, liabilities, equity, cash, debt, operating cash flow,
capex, and free cash flow for the most recent periods. Use when you
need fundamentals or growth trends.

Args:
    ticker: Stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL".
    quarterly: True for quarterly statements, False for annual.
    periods: How many recent periods to return (max about 4-5).

tools.name: get_news
tools.description:
Recent news articles about a company.

Each article has title, source, published_at, url, text (summary or
snippet), and provider. Use when you need recent events, sentiment,
or catalysts for a stock.

Args:
    ticker: Stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL".
    days: How far back to look (NewsAPI free plan caps at ~29 days).
    limit: Max articles to return.
    source: "auto" (NewsAPI + Yahoo, local CSV if both fail),
        "newsapi", "yahoo", or "local".

tools.name: get_news_digest
tools.description:
Short digest of recent news for a stock, built by the prompt chain.

Fetches, cleans, and dedupes recent articles, labels each by topic
(earnings, product, legal, macro, analyst_rating, other) and
sentiment, extracts key facts, and summarizes them. Returns
headline, summary (cites articles as [id]), catalysts, risks,
sentiment_counts, topic_counts, and sources. Use this instead of
get_news when you want the news already analyzed.

Args:
    ticker: Stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL".
    days: How far back to look.
    limit: Max articles to fetch before filtering (split across
        news sources).

tools.name: get_macro_snapshot
tools.description:
Current macroeconomic backdrop in one call.

Latest fed funds rate, 10-year Treasury yield, CPI inflation (year
over year %), unemployment rate, and VIX, each with the change versus
a year ago. Use when the analysis needs interest-rate, inflation, or
market-risk context.

tools.name: get_series
tools.description:
Observations for one FRED economic data series.

Common series: FEDFUNDS (fed funds rate), DGS10 (10y Treasury),
CPIAUCSL (CPI), UNRATE (unemployment), GDPC1 (real GDP), VIXCLS
(VIX). Use when you need the history of a specific indicator.

Args:
    series_id: FRED series id, e.g. "UNRATE".
    start: Start date YYYY-MM-DD (default: about 2 years ago).

tools.name: get_recent_filings
tools.description:
Recent SEC filings for a company, newest first.

Returns form type, filing date, period (report_date), and a URL to
the main document. 10-K = annual report, 10-Q = quarterly report,
8-K = material event (earnings releases, leadership changes, deals).
Use to find official disclosures, then get_filing_text to read one.

Args:
    ticker: Stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL".
    form: Comma-separated form types, or "any".
    limit: Max filings to return.

tools.name: get_filing_text
tools.description:
Plain text of an SEC filing document (retrieval tool).

Use after get_recent_filings to read what a filing says. Pass a
section heading to jump to it, e.g. "Risk Factors", "Management's
Discussion", "Results of Operations", or "Liquidity". Without a
section you get the start of the document.

Args:
    url: Document URL from get_recent_filings.
    section: Optional heading to jump to.
    max_chars: Max characters of text to return.

tools.name: get_earnings
tools.description:
Recent quarterly earnings: reported EPS vs. analyst estimate.

Each quarter has fiscal_date_ending, reported_date, reported_eps,
estimated_eps, surprise, and surprise_pct. Use to judge whether a
company has been beating or missing expectations.

Args:
    ticker: Stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL".
    quarters: Number of recent quarters to return.

---

## **APPLE INC. (AAPL) – INVESTMENT RESEARCH REPORT**

### **EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**
Apple is trading at $343.46 (as of October 16, 2026) with strong momentum and solid fundamentals, though valuation is elevated. The stock has delivered 36.6% returns over the past year and recently achieved a $5 trillion market capitalization. Management transition, strong product momentum (foldable iPhone sellout), and AI monetization opportunities present catalysts, but valuation multiples, tariff headwinds, and execution risks warrant caution.

**Recommendation: HOLD with selective accumulation on weakness**

---

## **1. PRICE MOMENTUM & TECHNICAL BACKDROP**

**Performance Summary:**
- **Last Close:** $343.46 (Oct 16, 2026)
- **52-Week Range:** $246.03 – $343.46 (current at 52-week high)
- **1-Year Return:** +36.6% (strong outperformance)
- **6-Month Return:** +27.3% (consistent momentum)
- **3-Month Return:** +5.3% (moderating gains)
- **1-Month Return:** +1.9% (flat after 1-year rally)
- **Annualized Volatility:** 24.47% (elevated but in line with large-cap tech)

**Technical Assessment:** AAPL has exhausted near-term momentum after a year-long rally, now trading near 52-week highs. The decelerating 3-month and 1-month returns suggest consolidation phase. At current levels, the stock faces resistance; any pullback toward $300-$320 would be healthier entry points.

---

## **2. COMPANY FUNDAMENTALS & VALUATION**
